newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firmer in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firmer in late trading.

text.p: Indonesia's rupiah was firmer against the dollar in late Tuesday trading, dealers said.
They said trading was lacklustre ahead of a public holiday on Wednesday. The market will reopen on Thursday.
One U.S. bank dealer said some operators were seen selling dollars in the afternoon to cash in on weekend premiums.

He said there was increased dollar buying at midday, sending the dollar to a high of 2,406.75, following reports of fresh violence in Pekalongan, central Java. But the rupiah later bounced back oin local buying. Troops were called out in the town when rival political supporters clashed, residents said.

Residents said hundreds of people who apparently were supporters of the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) attacked a housing estate mostly inhabited by civil servants late on Monday night. Civil servants are usually supporters of the ruling Golkar party.
Dealers said, however, local operators seemed to shrug off the fresh clashes and continued to counter dollar buying.
"The financial markets might be affected if things were happening in Jakarta or Surabaya," one said.
Dealers said they were expecting similar tensions ahead of the general election scheduled on May 29.
Spot rupiah was at 2,406.25/06.50 at 0850 GMT against an opening of 2,405.0/06.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,406.15/06.30 and 2,405.5/05.8, respectively.
Dealers said there was no real drive in the market and overall swap rates were softening on ample liquidity.
Tom/next swaps were at 0.20/0.28 and overnight at 0.5/0.6.
One-month swaps edged down to 11.5/12.0 from 12.50/12.75, two to 23.0/24.5 from 24.0/25.0, three to 34.5/35.5 from 35.0/35.5 and six to 71.5/72.0 from 71.5/72.5 points.
Bank Indonesia raised the intervention band by one point to 2,398/2,590 and the conversion band to 2,398/2,446 on Tuesday.
